evidence: Focal 2 mm x 2 mm low-grade cartilage defect in the weightbearing portion of the medial femoral condyle. Otherwise well maintained medial tibiofemoral hyaline articular cartilage.
Low-grade chondral thinning in the lateral tibiofemoral compartment.
Relatively well-maintained patellofemoral hyaline articular cartilage.
rationales: The focal medial femoral cartilage defect is explicitly low-grade and 2 by 2 mm, below the qualifying depth/region criterion; the remaining medial cartilage is well maintained. This is a report-level below-threshold negative using stated qualitative depth and measured extent, without importing a numeric grading framework.

The lateral tibiofemoral thinning is explicitly low-grade, supporting a below-threshold negative. Severe mucoid degeneration and complex tearing in the same compartment refer to the meniscus, not cartilage severity, and do not override the chondral qualifier.

Patellofemoral cartilage is only relatively well maintained. This qualified comparative preservation does not explicitly establish normal cartilage or the absence of a roughly1 cm region with greater-than50 percent loss. No separate depth/extent or unqualified normal PF assessment resolves that limitation; preserve uncertainty rather than infer a reliable negative or a positive.
